## The problem

Cattle in tropical and subtropical pasture systems routinely face periods of intense thermal stress. During the hottest hours of the day, animals face a behavioral trade-off: continue grazing and risk overheating, or seek shade and reduce dry matter intake.

When shade is not available — or when water access is restricted — this trade-off becomes a welfare problem. Animals may reduce voluntary grazing, increase time standing idle, or alter drinking patterns in ways that affect both productivity and wellbeing.

What is less understood is **how the combination of shade and water availability** — not either factor alone — shapes cattle behavior across a full 24-hour cycle. Nocturnal compensatory grazing, drinking dynamics, and body surface temperature responses to restricted resources are rarely studied together.

This experiment set out to answer that directly.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## The experiment

Thirty-two cows — half Braford, half Jersey — were assigned to four treatment combinations across a 4 × 4 Latin square design, managed under Voisin Rational Grazing in silvopastoral paddocks at the Ressacada Experimental Farm, UFSC.

```{=html}
<div class="treatment-grid">
  <div class="treatment-card shade">
    <div class="code">S+W+</div>
    <div class="label">Shade available<br>Water <em>ad libitum</em> 24h</div>
  </div>
  <div class="treatment-card shade">
    <div class="code">S+W−</div>
    <div class="label">Shade available<br>Water restricted to 1h/day</div>
  </div>
  <div class="treatment-card no-shade">
    <div class="code">S−W+</div>
    <div class="label">No shade<br>Water <em>ad libitum</em> 24h</div>
  </div>
  <div class="treatment-card no-shade">
    <div class="code">S−W−</div>
    <div class="label">No shade<br>Water restricted to 1h/day</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

Behavioral scans were recorded every 10 minutes across full 24-hour cycles. Thermographic images captured body surface temperatures at three time points daily. Black globe thermometers, soil surface measurements, and meteorological station data characterized the thermal environment continuously.

## Study context

This research was conducted under the **Voisin Rational Grazing** system, which structures pasture use around animal welfare and soil recovery. Shade trees (*Inga edulis*) were established in rows across experimental paddocks, creating a silvopastoral layout that mirrors real-world agroecological farm conditions in southern Brazil.

The experiment ran from **December 2021 to April 2022** — the hottest and most humid months of the year in Florianópolis — ensuring ecologically relevant thermal stress conditions throughout.

::: callout-note
This website accompanies a manuscript currently in preparation for submission to *Applied Animal Behaviour Science*. Data, analysis scripts, and the full methods are available in the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/jpdonadio/water-shade-cattle-behavior).
:::
